data.content_ref: inline:The target's defense collapses into the very induction it seeks to avoid because the 'methodological rule' to prefer better-corroborated theories for 'rapid error elimination' implicitly assumes that a theory which survived severe tests in the past is more likely to yield informative (i.e., non-refuted) results in the future than an untested one. If there is no inductive link between past survival and future performance, the choice between a well-corroborated theory and a new, bold conjecture is methodologically neutral regarding 'error elimination'; preferring the former solely because it worked before is an inductive wager on nature's uniformity, smuggling back the principle Popper rejected.
